key_insight: Combining AI slide analysis, predicted morphology, and manually assessed PRAME staining achieved similar malignancy discrimination to AI slide analysis alone.
clinical_relevance: The framework could help organize complementary evidence for melanocytic lesion assessment, but improved diagnostic accuracy or patient outcomes were not demonstrated.
method: Analyzed H&E whole-slide images using the Virchow2 foundation model and STAMP framework.
Trained models to predict malignancy and established histopathological features.
Combined AI predictions with manually assessed PRAME immunohistochemistry.
evidence_signal: In a retrospective cohort of 1,000 lesions, models trained on 800 cases achieved test AUROCs of 0.970 for standalone malignancy classification and 0.972 for the integrated model on 200 temporally held-out cases.
watch_item: Evaluation was limited to a retrospective cohort selected for PRAME testing; broader generalizability and prospective clinical utility remain unestablished.
paper_title: Integrating Histopathology Foundation Models and PRAME Immunohistochemistry in Melanoma Diagnosis
